next_step: Closed-lost. Capture notes, update playbook. Re-open in 6-12m if budget/champion returns.
lost_reason: Chose hyperscaler managed endpoints (Azure OpenAI + Azure infra) citing operational simplicity and existing MSFT enterprise discounts.
notes: Account profile: mid-sized ecommerce platform providing storefront + personalization to SMB brands.
Initial interest (Aug 2024): conversational support assistant + product personalization via embeddings. Highly latency-sensitive for cart flows.
Aug 2024 - Discovery call with CTO and Head of ML. They asked about on-prem options; primary constraint was data residency for EU customers.
Sep 2024 - Security questionnaire submitted; CISO flagged KMS + audit trail requirements. Asked for SOC2 + formal pen test results.
Oct 2024 - POC kickoff: small production-like load on dedicated pool. Goal: 99th percentile token latency < 200ms for chat; embedding throughput 200 qps.
POC feedback (Nov 2024): performance met targets, cost slightly higher than internal projections. SE recommended batching + quantized model profile to reduce cost.
Dec 2024 - Pricing deck shared (drive link). Amberflow requested committed pricing; procurement asked for 12-month price lock.
Jan 2025 - Procurement pressure: CFO exploring hyperscaler discounts through enterprise Azure agreement. Started parallel eval of Azure OpenAI/Managed Endpoints.
Mar 2025 - Security deep-dive. CISO required HSM-backed key management and formal ISO27001 evidence. Redwood provided SOC2 + KMS integration notes; CISO remained unconvinced.
Jun 2025 - Internal re-org at Amberflow: ML platform team lost sponsor (Director left). No clear internal champion to drive procurement with Redwood.
Sep-Oct 2025 - Competitive push: Azure team presented integrated billing, compliance guarantees, and free migration credits. Procurement favored single-vendor consolidation.
Nov 2025 - Final decision: Amberflow selected Azure-managed endpoints (Azure OpenAI + Azure infra) citing easier procurement, consolidated SLAs, and discounting. Officially closed-lost.
Quote from CTO on final call: 'We need the path of least resistance for procurement and operations. Azure gives us that today.'
Internal next actions: archive opportunities, keep security Q/A artifacts in knowledge base, flag for re-engagement if champion returns or if multi-cloud requirements emerge.
Lessons learned: emphasize migration playbook vs hyperscaler, pre-package HSM/KMS compliance evidence, create commercial offset options for enterprise Azure partnerships.
public_notes: key blocker: no internal champion after org change
budget/procurement: Azure discounts won the deal
security: CISO wanted ISO27001/HSM; SOC2 + KMS notes insufficient
POC: succeeded technically but cost + procurement risk dominated decision
